Joshua Harris
JOSH-oo-uh HAIR-is
proper noun
American author (b. 1974) of I Kissed Dating Goodbye, who later renounced his book, his ministry, and the Christian faith.

📖 Biblical Definition

Joshua Harris is the American author who, as a young man in the 1990s, wrote the enormously popular courtship book I Kissed Dating Goodbye and pastored a prominent church, and who in 2019 publicly renounced his book, announced the end of his marriage, and declared that he was no longer a Christian. The dictionary records his story soberly, not to mock a man but to learn from a warning. The case illustrates the difference between a profession of faith and the possession of it, and the bitter end of public deconstruction. Scripture is plain that not all who are numbered with the church are truly of it: they went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us. The seed sown on stony ground springs up quickly and withers when tribulation or persecution arises, having no root in itself. The just shall live by faith, but the soul that draws back, God’s soul has no pleasure in; and no man, having put his hand to the plough and looking back, is fit for the kingdom. The dictionary names Harris’s apostasy as a grief and a caution: a reminder that early influence and even genuine-seeming ministry are no substitute for a root in Christ, that perseverance to the end is the mark of true grace, and that the church must build her young not on the latest movement but on the unchanging gospel.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

American author of I Kissed Dating Goodbye who in 2019 renounced his book, marriage, and the Christian faith; a sober warning on profession without possession and the end of deconstruction.

📖 Key Scripture

1Jo 2:19 — "They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us."

Mat 13:21 — "Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended."

Heb 10:38 — "Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him."

Luk 9:62 — "And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Public “deconstruction” is celebrated as honesty and growth; Scripture names the falling away of one who had no root as apostasy, and holds that perseverance is the mark of true grace.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption to name is the celebration of public deconstruction—the renouncing of the faith paraded as a brave and healthy journey of growth, the apostate honored for his honesty. Harris’s public departure was widely praised in just these terms. But Scripture will not call apostasy maturity. The falling away of one who once professed and even ministered is not enlightenment but the manifesting of a faith that had no root; they went out from us because they were not of us. To rebrand abandonment of Christ as authenticity is to flatter the very ruin of a soul.

The principle to recover is perseverance as the mark of true grace and the necessity of a root in Christ. Genuine faith endures; the just shall live by faith, and the soul that draws back, God has no pleasure in. The seed on stony ground springs up fast and withers fast, having no root; early popularity, a bestselling book, even a pastorate, are no substitute for being truly rooted in Christ. The dictionary records Harris’s case not to despair—for God can yet recover the wanderer—but as a solemn caution to build the young on the unchanging gospel, and to pray that profession may prove to be possession, persevering to the end.
